literal: Burial was at Jinling.
idiomatic: She was buried at Jinling.

literal: In the first year of Chenming her title and posthumous name were elevated, and she received joint offerings in the imperial temple.
idiomatic: In Chenming year 1 her honors and posthumous title were raised, and she was given joint sacrifice in the ancestral temple.

literal: Empress Zhen of Emperor Wen, the Lin clan, was a native of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: Empress Zhen of Emperor Wen, née Lin, came from Pingyuan.

literal: [12] Her uncle Jinlu rose from the eunuch ranks, won favor with Empress Dowager Chang, and reached the posts of Master of Writing and Duke of Pingliang.
idiomatic: [12] Her uncle Jinlu had risen from the eunuch service, won favor with Empress Dowager Chang, and rose to Master of Writing and Duke of Pingliang.

literal: Jinlu's elder brother Sheng was administrator of Pingliang.
idiomatic: Jinlu's elder brother Sheng served as administrator of Pingliang.

literal: Jinlu, at the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's reign, was regional inspector of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xianzu's reign Jinlu was made regional inspector of Dingzhou.

literal: Before long he was executed by Yi Hun, and the brothers all died.
idiomatic: Soon afterward he was killed by Yi Hun, and the brothers all perished.

literal: Sheng had no sons but two daughters, who entered the inner palace.
idiomatic: Sheng had no sons; his two daughters were sent into the inner palace.

literal: The empress was beautiful in face and form, won Gaozu's favor, and bore the prince Xun.
idiomatic: The empress was strikingly beautiful, found favor with Emperor Gaozu, and bore Prince Xun.

literal: Because Xun was to be heir apparent, in the seventh year of Taihe the empress died according to the old custom.
idiomatic: As Xun was to be crown prince, in Taihe year 7 the empress died under the old custom.

literal: Gaozu was humane and forbearing and did not wish to repeat former deeds, yet he followed Empress Dowager Wenming's intent, so it was not carried out.
idiomatic: Gaozu was merciful and unwilling to repeat the old practice, but he deferred to Empress Dowager Wenming, and the custom was not enforced.

literal: Her posthumous title was Empress Zhen, and she was buried at Jinling.
idiomatic: She was given the posthumous name Empress Zhen and buried at Jinling.

literal: When Xun was ordered to die for his crimes, the authorities memorialized to strip the empress posthumously and reduce her to commoner status.
idiomatic: After Xun was condemned and ordered to die, the authorities petitioned to posthumously depose the empress as a commoner.

literal: The deposed empress of Emperor Wen, the Feng clan, was a daughter of Grand Preceptor Xi.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen's deposed empress, née Feng, was a daughter of Grand Preceptor Xi.

literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe, after Gaozu had completed mourning, Grand Commandant Yuan Pi and others memorialized that the office of the empress had not been established and the six palaces had no mistress, asking that the inner rank be settled.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 17, once Gaozu had finished mourning, Grand Commandant Yuan Pi and others submitted that with no empress installed and the six palaces without a head, the inner court should be regularized.

literal: Gaozu assented and installed her as empress.
idiomatic: Gaozu agreed and made her empress.

literal: Whenever Gaozu observed ritual, the empress and consorts and concubines below all attended him in turn.
idiomatic: Gaozu always kept to ritual: the empress, consorts, and lower concubines all came to him in proper order.

literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, the empress remained in the capital.
idiomatic: On the southern campaigns the empress stayed behind in the capital.

literal: When Gaozu campaigned south again, the empress led the six palaces in moving to Luoyang.
idiomatic: On another southern expedition the empress led the six palaces in relocating to Luoyang.

literal: When the empress's father Xi and elder brother Dan died, Gaozu wrote letters of consolation expressing his grief.
idiomatic: When her father Xi and elder brother Dan died, Gaozu wrote to console her and voice his sorrow.

literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, her favor was very great.
idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, she enjoyed exceptional favor.

literal: Later Gaozu again summoned the empress's elder sister, a lady of bright demeanor, to Luoyang; she gradually won favor, and the empress's courtesy and affection waned.
idiomatic: Later Gaozu brought the empress's elder sister, already a zhaoyi, back to Luoyang; as the sister gained favor, the empress's standing slowly faded.

literal: The zhaoyi considered herself older and having entered the palace earlier, was long treated with regard, looked down on the empress, and would not observe a concubine's rites.
idiomatic: The zhaoyi, being older and having entered the palace earlier, had long been favored; she slighted the empress and refused the deference owed a junior wife.

literal: Though the empress was not jealous by nature, at times she showed shame and resentment.
idiomatic: Though not jealous by nature, the empress sometimes showed shame and bitterness.

literal: The zhaoyi plotted to become mistress of the inner court and slandered her in every way.
idiomatic: The zhaoyi schemed to rule the inner palace and wove slander on every side.

literal: Before long the empress was deposed to commoner status.
idiomatic: Soon the empress was deposed and reduced to a commoner.

literal: The empress was chaste, careful, and possessed moral conduct; she then became a nun in plain practice.
idiomatic: Chaste and principled, she took the tonsure as a nun in austere practice.

literal: Later she died at Yaoguang Buddhist Temple.
idiomatic: She ended her days at Yaoguang Temple.

literal: Empress You of Emperor Wen was also a daughter of Feng Xi.
idiomatic: Empress You of Emperor Wen was likewise a daughter of Feng Xi.

literal: Her mother was the Chang clan, originally of low station; she won Xi's favor, and after Xi's primary consort the princess died, she took charge of the household.
idiomatic: Her mother, née Chang, was of humble birth; favored by Xi, after his principal consort the princess died she managed the household.

literal: She bore the empress and Beiping Duke Su.
idiomatic: She bore the future empress and Beiping Duke Su.

literal: Grand Empress Dowager Wenming wished the family honored and favored, so she selected both of Xi's daughters to enter the inner palace; they were fourteen.
idiomatic: Grand Empress Dowager Wenming wanted the Feng house ennobled, so both of Xi's daughters were chosen for the inner palace at age fourteen.

literal: One died early.
idiomatic: One of them died young.

literal: The empress had charm and grace and was especially loved and favored.
idiomatic: The empress was alluring and won special favor.

literal: Before long she fell ill; Empress Dowager Wenming sent her home to become a nun, yet Gaozu still kept her in mind.
idiomatic: Soon she fell ill; Empress Dowager Wenming sent her home to take the veil, though Gaozu still thought of her.

literal: After a year and more the empress dowager died.
idiomatic: A little over a year later the empress dowager died.

literal: When Gaozu finished mourning he still sought her; hearing her chronic rash had cleared, he sent the eunuch Shuang Sannian with an imperial letter of inquiry and welcomed her to Luoyang.
idiomatic: After mourning ended Gaozu still sought her; learning her chronic rash had healed, he sent the eunuch Shuang Sannian with an imperial message and had her brought to Luoyang.

literal: When she arrived, favor exceeded the first time; she alone shared his bed each night, and palace women rarely saw him again.
idiomatic: On her arrival favor surpassed the first reign; she alone shared his nights, and other palace women seldom gained audience.

literal: She was appointed left zhaoyi, then later installed as empress.
idiomatic: She was made left zhaoyi and later elevated to empress.

literal: From the time she had returned home for illness there had been talk of misconduct; with Gaozu campaigning south year after year, the empress then had a secret affair with the palace attendant Gaopusa.
idiomatic: Rumors of misconduct had followed her illness and return home; while Gaozu campaigned south year after year, she took the palace attendant Gaopusa as her lover.

literal: When Gaozu was unwell at Runan, the empress then openly indulged in shameless license, and regular palace attendants Shuang Meng and others were her confidants.
idiomatic: When Gaozu fell ill at Runan, the empress flaunted her debauchery, with Regular Palace Attendant Shuang Meng and others as her inner circle.

literal: Regular Palace Attendant Ju Peng remonstrated but she would not listen; in anger and fear he died.
idiomatic: Regular Palace Attendant Ju Peng admonished her in vain and, stricken with anger and dread, died.

literal: At that time Princess Pengcheng, wife of the son of Prince of Song Liu Chang, was young and widowed.
idiomatic: Princess Pengcheng, daughter-in-law of Prince of Song Liu Chang, was young and living as a widow.

literal: Beiping Duke Feng Su, the empress's younger brother by the same mother, sought marriage through the empress; Gaozu consented.
idiomatic: Beiping Duke Feng Su, her full brother, sought her help in marrying the princess; Gaozu agreed.

literal: The princess was unwilling in heart; the empress wished to force the matter.
idiomatic: The princess refused, but the empress meant to compel her.

literal: The wedding day was near when the princess secretly took a dozen or so maids and household servants in a light carriage, braved torrential rain, went to Xuanchi to audience Gaozu, stated her true intent, and reported the empress's affair with Pusa.
idiomatic: With the wedding set, the princess secretly took a light carriage with a dozen maids and servants, rode through driving rain to Xuanchi to see Gaozu, declared her refusal, and revealed the empress's liaison with Pusa.

literal: Gaozu heard this in shock and alarm, did not wholly believe it, and kept it secret; only Prince of Pengcheng attending his illness at his side knew the whole affair.
idiomatic: Gaozu was stunned but did not fully believe her and kept the matter hidden; only Prince of Pengcheng, at his sickbed, knew everything.

literal: Thereafter the empress grew anxious and fearful; with her mother the Chang clan she sought witches, performing every prayer and curse, wishing Gaozu's illness would not lift so that one day, like Empress Dowager Wenming aiding a young ruler and holding power, she might reward them beyond measure.
idiomatic: Afterward the empress grew fearful; with her mother Lady Chang she turned to witches and every form of curse-prayer, hoping Gaozu would not recover so she could rule as regent like Empress Dowager Wenming and repay them lavishly.

literal: She also took the three sacrificial animals for illicit shrines in the palace, claiming prayers for blessing while devoted to heterodox ways.
idiomatic: She set up illicit shrines in the palace with the three sacrificial beasts, pretending to pray for blessings while practicing forbidden rites.

literal: Mother Chang sometimes came to the palace herself, sometimes sent maids to exchange messages.
idiomatic: Lady Chang sometimes entered the palace herself, sometimes sent maids to carry messages back and forth.

literal: When Gaozu traveled north from Yuzhou to Ye, the empress feared returning to face investigation, grew ever more terrified, and repeatedly had eunuchs convey greetings on her behalf, all rewarded with garments and earnestly entrusted not to let anything leak.
idiomatic: As Gaozu went north from Yuzhou to Ye, the empress, dreading investigation on his return, sent eunuchs again and again with greetings, lavished clothes on them, and begged them to keep silent.

literal: She also had Shuang Meng go along to see whether they were trustworthy.
idiomatic: She also sent Shuang Meng to go with them and test their loyalty.

literal: [13] Yet only junior yellow-gate attendant Su Xingshou secretly reported the details; Gaozu questioned him on the full story and ordered that it not be divulged.
idiomatic: [13] Only junior yellow-gate attendant Su Xingshou secretly laid out the whole affair; Gaozu questioned him to the bottom and commanded secrecy.

literal: At Luoyang, Pusa, Shuang Meng, and six others were seized and questioned; they testified against one another in turn, and the full circumstances were obtained.
idiomatic: At Luoyang six men including Pusa and Shuang Meng were arrested; their mutual accusations brought the whole truth to light.

literal: Gaozu, ill and resting in the warming chamber, summoned the empress at night and had Pusa and the others lined up outside the door.
idiomatic: Gaozu, ill in the warming chamber, summoned the empress by night and lined Pusa and the others outside the door.

literal: As the empress was about to enter, he ordered eunuchs to search her garments; the slightest blade meant execution.
idiomatic: Before she entered he ordered eunuchs to search her; any blade, however small, meant death.

literal: The empress kowtowed and wept in apology; then she was granted a seat on the eastern pillar, more than two zhang from the imperial mat.
idiomatic: She kowtowed and wept; then she was given a seat by the eastern pillar, more than two zhang from his couch.

literal: Gaozu had Pusa and the others state the facts, then reproached the empress: "Your mother practices sorcery—you must tell it fully.
idiomatic: Gaozu made Pusa and the others confess, then rebuked the empress: "Your mother uses witchcraft—speak of it in full.

literal: " The empress begged to dismiss those present and had something to report in secret.
idiomatic: " She begged to dismiss attendants and speak privately.

literal: Gaozu ordered all central attendants out, keeping only Director of the Long Autumn Bureau Bai Zheng at his side, took a guard's straight blade and held it upright; the empress still would not speak.
idiomatic: Gaozu sent the central attendants away, keeping only Director of the Long Autumn Bai Zheng beside him with a guard's blade held upright; still she would not speak.

literal: Gaozu then stuffed Bai Zheng's ears tightly with cotton, called to Zheng softly again and again, and getting no answer, ordered the empress to speak.
idiomatic: Gaozu stuffed cotton into Zheng's ears, whispered his name repeatedly without reply, and then commanded the empress to speak.

literal: The matter was concealed; no one knew it.
idiomatic: What she said remained hidden; no one else knew.

literal: Gaozu then summoned the princes of Pengcheng and Beihai to enter and sit, saying: "Once she was your sister-in-law; now she is another's person—enter and do not shrink.
idiomatic: Gaozu called in the princes of Pengcheng and Beihai and said: "Once she was your sister-in-law; now she is a stranger—come in and do not hold back.

literal: " The two princes firmly declined but could not refuse the command.
idiomatic: " Both princes refused but could not disobey.

literal: When they entered, Gaozu said: "This old woman meant to drive a bare blade into my ribs!
idiomatic: Once inside Gaozu said: "This old woman meant to put a blade in my ribs!

literal: Question her to the end on how it began and ended; hold nothing back.
idiomatic: Press her for the full story and spare nothing.

literal: " Gaozu deeply blamed himself and expressed shame before the two princes.
idiomatic: " Gaozu took the blame upon himself and apologized to the two princes.

literal: He also said: "The Feng girl cannot again be deposed and driven out; for now let her sit idle in the palace—if she has the heart she can die by herself. Do not think I still have affection.
idiomatic: He added: "The Feng girl will not be deposed again; let her sit empty in the palace—if she has the will she can die herself. Do not imagine I still care.

literal: " Gaozu was by nature most filial; still for Empress Dowager Wenming's sake he did not yet carry out deposition.
idiomatic: " Filial as he was, he still would not depose her out of regard for Empress Dowager Wenming.

literal: After a long while the two princes withdrew, and he then gave the empress a parting message before death.
idiomatic: After a long while the princes left, and he sent the empress a final farewell.

literal: [14] She bowed again, touched her head to the ground, and wept with sobs and sighs.
idiomatic: [14] She bowed again to the ground, weeping and sighing.

literal: He ordered her into the eastern room.
idiomatic: He had her enter the eastern chamber.

literal: After she entered the palace, the emperor ordered a eunuch to question the empress; the empress cursed: "I am the Son of Heaven's wife—should I face him in person, or have you relay words!
idiomatic: After she was inside, the emperor sent a eunuch to question her; she raged: "I am the emperor's wife—should I not speak to him face to face rather than through you!

literal: " Gaozu was angry and ordered the empress's mother Chang to enter and beat her with rods; Chang flogged her more than a hundred times before stopping.
idiomatic: " Gaozu in anger summoned her mother Lady Chang to beat her with rods; Chang lashed her more than a hundred strokes before stopping.

literal: Gaozu soon campaigned south; the empress remained in the capital. Though she had lost favor for her crimes, ladies and concubines still served her according to ritual; only Crown Prince Xuanzong in the eastern palace was barred from court audiences.
idiomatic: Gaozu soon marched south again; though disgraced, she was still treated by consorts according to rite, while Crown Prince Xuanzong in the eastern palace was forbidden court audiences.

literal: When Gaozu was gravely ill he told Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "The inner palace has long violated feminine virtue and cut itself off from Heaven.
idiomatic: Near death Gaozu told Prince of Pengcheng Xie: "The inner palace has long violated its proper virtue and turned from Heaven.

literal: If we do not deal with this early, I fear it will become the story of the late Han.
idiomatic: If we do not act soon, I fear another tale like the end of Han.

literal: After my death, grant her suicide in a separate palace and bury her with empress rites, that the Feng house's great fault may be covered.
idiomatic: After I die, let her take poison in a separate palace and bury her with empress honors, to cover the Feng clan's shame.

literal: " When Gaozu died and the coffin reached Luyang, the testament was then carried out.
idiomatic: " When Gaozu died and the coffin reached Luyang, his final testament was executed.

literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang, carrying out the testament, and Director of the Long Autumn Bai Zheng and others entered to give the empress poison; she ran shouting and refused to take her leave, saying: "Would the ruler truly do this? It is those princes killing me!
idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang proclaimed the testament; Bai Zheng and others brought poison; she fled shouting and would not die, crying: "Would the throne do this? Those princes are killing me!

literal: " Zheng and the others seized her, forced her, and she took pepper poison and expired.
idiomatic: " They seized her, forced the dose, and she died from the poison.

literal: She was laid out with empress rites.
idiomatic: She was buried with empress honors.

literal: When the coffin halted south of Luoyang, Prince of Xianyang Xi and others learned she was truly dead and said to one another: "Without the testament we brothers would also have had to scheme to remove her—how could we let a woman of misconduct rule the realm and kill us?
idiomatic: When the coffin paused south of Luoyang, Prince of Xianyang Xi and others learned she was dead and said to one another: "Without the testament we would have removed her ourselves—how could a disgraced woman rule the realm and destroy us?

literal: " Her posthumous title was Empress You, and she was buried within the precinct of Changling.
idiomatic: " She was posthumously named Empress You and buried within Changling.

literal: Empress Zhao of Emperor Wen, the Gao clan, was a younger sister of Duke of the State as Minister of Education Zhao.
idiomatic: Empress Zhao of Emperor Wen, née Gao, was a sister of Minister of Education Zhao, Duke of the State.

literal: Her father Yang; her mother the Ge clan; in all four sons and three daughters, all born in the eastern frontier.
idiomatic: Her father was Yang; her mother was of the Ge clan; they had four sons and three daughters, all born in the eastern marches.

literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign the whole family moved west; reaching Longcheng garrison, the garrison reported the empress's virtue, beauty, and gentle charm, fit to fill the palace.
idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign the family moved west; at Longcheng garrison the commandant reported her grace and beauty, fit for the inner palace.

literal: When she arrived, Empress Dowager Wenming personally visited the northern bureau, saw the empress's looks, marveled, and had her enter the inner palace at age thirteen.
idiomatic: On arrival Empress Dowager Wenming visited the northern bureau herself, marveled at her looks, and sent her into the inner palace at thirteen.

literal: Earlier, when young, the empress once dreamed she stood in a hall while sunlight from the window shone on her, blazing hot; she dodged east and west, yet the light still slanted upon her without cease.
idiomatic: As a girl she dreamed she stood in a hall while sunlight poured through the window, burning hot; she dodged east and west, but the light still found her.

literal: Thus for several nights; the empress thought it strange and told her father Yang; Yang asked Min Zong of Liaodong.
idiomatic: For several nights she wondered at it and told her father Yang, who consulted Min Zong of Liaodong.

literal: Zong said: "This is a strange omen; nobility beyond words.
idiomatic: Min Zong said: "This is a rare sign—honor beyond speech.

literal: " Yang said: "How do you know?
idiomatic: " Yang asked: "How can you tell?

literal: " Zong said: "The sun is the virtue of a ruler, the image of emperors and kings.
idiomatic: " He said: "The sun is the ruler's virtue, the sign of sovereignty.

literal: Light shining on a woman's body means favor and command will reach her.
idiomatic: Light on a woman means imperial favor will find her.

literal: That she dodged yet was still lit means the sovereign will come seeking her and she will have no choice.
idiomatic: That she dodged yet was still lit means the lord will seek her and she cannot refuse.

literal: In old times one dreamed the moon entered her womb and still bore a Son of Heaven—how much more a sign of sunlight.
idiomatic: Once a woman dreamed the moon entered her womb and bore a Son of Heaven—how much more sunlight.

literal: This girl will surely receive the imperial mandate and bear the image of one who nurtures a ruler.
idiomatic: This girl will receive the imperial mandate and bear a ruler of men.

literal: " She then bore Xuanzong.
idiomatic: " She bore Xuanzong.

literal: Later she bore Prince of Guangping Huai, then Princess Changle.
idiomatic: Later she bore Prince of Guangping Huai, then Princess Changle.

literal: When Lady Feng the zhaoyi's favor flourished, she secretly intended to mother and raise Xuanzong; the empress went herself to Luoyang and suddenly died at Gong county in Ji commandery—some say the zhaoyi sent men to assassinate the empress.
idiomatic: When Feng the zhaoyi rose in favor and plotted to raise Xuanzong as her own, the empress went to Luoyang and died suddenly at Gong in Ji commandery—some said the zhaoyi had her murdered.
